reference.source: Nelson Textbook of Pediatrics / standard medical genetics references
clinicalPearls: Most common inherited cause of intellectual disability and the leading single-gene contributor to autism spectrum disorder
Affected boys are typically more severely impaired than girls because of X-linkage, with variable expression in female carriers
Characteristic physical features include a long narrow face, prominent forehead and jaw, large protruding ears, and macro-orchidism that becomes evident around puberty
Behavioural profile often includes hyperactivity, attention problems, anxiety, hand-flapping, poor eye contact, and tactile defensiveness
Connective tissue laxity may produce joint hypermobility, flat feet, and mitral valve prolapse
Caused by expansion of a CGG trinucleotide repeat in the FMR1 gene leading to loss of the FMRP protein needed for normal synaptic function
Repeat number distinguishes normal, intermediate, premutation, and full-mutation alleles, with premutations carrying separate adult risks
Diagnosis is confirmed by targeted DNA testing (repeat sizing and methylation analysis) rather than routine karyotype
reference.pathophysiology: Fragile X syndrome results from an unstable expansion of a CGG trinucleotide repeat in the 5' untranslated region of the FMR1 gene on the X chromosome. When the repeat expands beyond the full-mutation threshold, the gene becomes hypermethylated and transcriptionally silenced, so little or no fragile X mental retardation protein (FMRP) is produced. FMRP normally regulates translation of numerous messenger RNAs at synapses, and its absence disrupts synaptic maturation and pruning, producing intellectual disability and the behavioural phenotype. Premutation-length repeats are not silenced but generate excess, potentially toxic FMR1 messenger RNA, which underlies the distinct premutation-associated disorders. The repeat tends to expand across generations, particularly through the maternal line, explaining anticipation.
additionalDifferentials: Sotos syndrome and other overgrowth syndromes
Nonspecific developmental delay of undetermined cause
additionalInvestigations: Targeted FMR1 molecular testing with CGG repeat sizing and methylation status
Chromosomal microarray if the molecular test is negative and the cause remains unclear
Formal developmental, cognitive, and autism assessments
Cardiac evaluation for mitral valve prolapse when clinically indicated
Genetic counselling and cascade testing of at-risk relatives
redFlags: Female premutation carriers face increased risk of primary ovarian insufficiency and reduced fertility
Older premutation carriers, particularly men, may develop fragile X-associated tremor/ataxia syndrome
Recurrence risk in the family is high, making prompt genetic counselling important
Emerging seizures or marked behavioural deterioration warrant neurological review
reference.prognosis: Life expectancy is generally normal, but intellectual disability persists lifelong; early behavioural, educational, and speech interventions improve functional outcomes, and severity is typically greater in males than in females.
pitfalls: Assuming a normal karyotype excludes the diagnosis when specific FMR1 repeat testing is required
Overlooking milder or subtle presentations in female carriers
Failing to recognise premutation-related adult conditions in relatives
Neglecting genetic counselling and cascade screening after diagnosis
